intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

messages.content:
Analyze a completed episode using ONLY released feedback and actual image/tool evidence.
Two INDEPENDENT tasks: (A) attribute previously ACTIVATED skills; [] if none.
(B) discover new procedural operations. Empty skill memory NEVER prevents discovery.
Short successful trajectories can contain useful operations. Correct final labels do NOT validate
all intermediate claims. Wrong final labels do NOT prove a proposed repair would work.
Identify one observed decision event: tool_disagreement, scope_gap, output_boundary,
targeted_verification, tool_parameter_repair, evidence_sufficient_stop, other, or none.
Separate OBSERVED operation from an UNEXECUTED HYPOTHESIS. A hypothesis is stored but not activated.
Do not infer lesions from yes/no labels, interpret classifier scores as severity, or use image mean
intensity as a clinical laterality rule. Do not invent a causal success story from final correctness.
Give CREATE for a supported reusable operation, PATCH for a supported refinement of an existing
snapshot skill, or NONE with a specific missing-evidence/triviality reason. No CREATE quota.
General: domain-agnostic process; task_level: task/tool routing; action_level: one tool interface.
Return JSON:
{"skill_adoption":[{"skill_id":"...","status":"ADOPTED_POSITIVE|ADOPTED_NEGATIVE|IGNORED",
"step_index":0,"evidence":"observable executed action"}],
"event_type":"...","evidence_steps":[0],"support_level":"observed|hypothesis|none",
"observed_operation":"...","proposed_operation":"...","trigger":"...",
"stop_condition":"...","extracted_pattern":"...","output_intent":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE",
"none_reason":null,"patch_target_id":null,"branch":"general|task_level|action_level"}.
Use ONLY activated_skill_ids for attribution; candidate retrieval alone is not activation or adoption.
Each attributed ID once. No hypothetical counterfactual claims. All step indices are zero based.

If PATCH is proposed, cite an ID from patch_candidates and its relevant procedure.
Distinguish detection of a finding from identifying its side. In an A-versus-B
localization item a bare yes/no does not identify either option. Check whether
observed outputs distinguish the options before treating a stop as supported.
Record an unexecuted tool repair as a hypothesis, even if it sounds plausible.

For a specific discordance in which the targeted expert is unambiguously negative and the grounded report lists a finding/box on the same image, do not count an interpolative roi_crop, zoom, crop, or coordinate box as confirmation of the finding; those add no acquired detail and do not independently resolve presence. Resolve the discordance with at most one independent reader asked the same binary presence question on the same full image using a registered tool capable of that read, if available. If no such independent reader is available, if it does not add acquired detail, or if it remains ambiguous, apply the fallback rule for a forced binary format: do not upgrade the clear targeted-expert negative read to positive solely on a single unverified generative finding/box. Stop after the allowed independent read or fallback is applied and do not loop with further crops. If the answer format permits an unknown/insufficient-evidence response and the conflict remains unresolved after the allowed independent read, return that; if the format does not permit it, use the fallback rule rather than declaring an unavailable unknown."}

Before querying, the expert prompt must name the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, anchored to source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification; the list must be sufficiently comprehensive for the question's scope. Required tool capabilities: a chest-radiograph expert QA model that accepts an explicit abnormality-list question, and an independent grounded-report/report-generation tool for the same image that returns a report or 'no significant findings'. Exclusions: do not apply to laterality/side questions, non-chest-radiograph images, or questions about a specific single finding where broad-system absence is not at issue. Do not use a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box to resolve side. Do not treat an incomplete abnormality list, a single negative model output, or a report limited to unrelated findings as evidence of absence. Stopping/unknown: stop and select the negative option only when both tools complete and concordantly report absence of the named cardiovascular abnormalities and the independent report explicitly supports no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings for the same image. If these concordant-absence conditions hold, select the negative option and stop. 6) If either call fails or is unavailable, if the report is ambiguous, if the named list is incomplete, or if outputs conflict, do not infer absence. For a conflict about the same finding and image, allow at most one targeted observed verification using a registered tool; if unresolved, stop and report uncertainty rather than asserting absence."}, Before querying, the expert prompt must name the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, anchored to source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification; the list must be sufficiently comprehensive for the question's scope. Required tool capabilities: a chest-radiograph expert QA model that accepts an explicit abnormality-list question, and an independent grounded-report/report-generation tool for the same image that returns a report or 'no significant findings'. Do not use a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box to resolve side. Do not treat an incomplete abnormality list, a single negative model output, or a report limited to unrelated findings as evidence of absence. Stopping/unknown: stop and select the negative option only when both tools complete and concordantly report absence of the named cardiovascular abnormalities and the independent report explicitly supports no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings for the same image. Convert the approved source analysis into ONE reusable procedural skill or a local patch.
Only source observations support the content. No fixed source answer, option letter, figure number or patient identity.
Trigger must specify applicability. core_action must specify observable checks, appropriate tool actions, failure/unknown
handling and when to stop; never require access to the current task's unknown reference answer.
Return JSON {"operation":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE","patch_target_id":null,"patch_section":null,"patch_content":null,
"content":{"name":"...","description":"...","applicable_conditions":"...","branch":"general|task_level|action_level",
"tool_name":null,"task_category":"provided category","required_tools":[],"risk_level":"low|medium|high","core_action":"..."}}.
For PATCH only return patch_target_id, patch_section (one content field), patch_content and operation;
do not replace unrelated sections. Scope fields branch, task_category and tool_name cannot change.
NONE may omit all other fields. Registered tools only. No invented measurements or blanket disease exclusion.

R54: Include explicit question-type/object requirements, triggering evidence,
exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.
Preserve the original nine-field content schema. Do not add fields or thresholds without source support.
If supplied reviewer feedback, perform ONE targeted repair: remove unsupported details or narrow scope.
Do not add evidence, change CREATE to PATCH or change an existing PATCH target during repair.

For laterality use an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome. A
bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone cannot resolve side. Treat
conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

message.content: {"operation":"PATCH","patch_target_id":"s_a3ec4f056cf659b7","patch_section":"core_action","patch_content":"1) Confirm the question is a binary disease/abnormality presence question about a specific named anatomical structure or region (for example, trachea or abdomen) on a chest image; if it asks side/laterality, localization, extent, severity, comparison, or is global/multi-structure, stop and do not apply this skill. 2) Ask the targeted expert the exact structure- or region-specific presence question and record whether the answer is a clear yes/no or ambiguous. 3) If using a broader grounded report for corroboration, inspect its findings/report for an explicit statement about that same named structure or region. A generic report such as 'No significant findings.' with zero grounded boxes does not explicitly cover a named region such as the abdomen; statements about lungs, heart, mediastinum, pleura, or skeleton are not target-region confirmation. 4) If the report explicitly addresses the same structure or region and agrees, cite it as corroboration; if it conflicts, do not claim concordance and perform at most one targeted observed verification if available. 5) If the report omits the structure or region, mark it as non-corroborating for that structure or region and rely only on a clear targeted-expert answer, or perform at most one additional targeted structure- or region-explicit check if available; do not describe the report as confirming absence for that structure or region. 6) If the targeted answer is unclear or fails and no report explicitly covers the structure or region, stop and state unknown/insufficient evidence rather than inferring from unrelated normal findings. Stop when the targeted expert is clear and any cited corroborating report explicitly covers the queried structure or region without conflict, or when unknown/insufficient evidence is declared."}

Convert the approved source analysis into ONE reusable procedural skill or a local patch.
Only source observations support the content. No fixed source answer, option letter, figure number or patient identity.
Trigger must specify applicability. core_action must specify observable checks, appropriate tool actions, failure/unknown
handling and when to stop; never require access to the current task's unknown reference answer.

For PATCH only return patch_target_id, patch_section (one content field), patch_content and operation;
do not replace unrelated sections. Scope fields branch, task_category and tool_name cannot change.
NONE may omit all other fields. Registered tools only. No invented measurements or blanket disease exclusion.

exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.
Preserve the original nine-field content schema. Do not add fields or thresholds without source support.
If supplied reviewer feedback, perform ONE targeted repair: remove unsupported details or narrow scope.
Do not add evidence, change CREATE to PATCH or change an existing PATCH target during repair.

For laterality use an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome. A
bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone cannot resolve side. Treat
conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

Before querying, the expert prompt must name the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, anchored to source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification; the list must be sufficiently comprehensive for the question's scope. Required tool capabilities: a chest-radiograph expert QA model that accepts an explicit abnormality-list question, and an independent grounded-report/report-generation tool for the same image that returns a report or 'no significant findings'. Exclusions: do not apply to laterality/side questions, non-chest-radiograph images, or questions about a specific single finding where broad-system absence is not at issue. Do not use a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box to resolve side. Do not treat an incomplete abnormality list, a single negative model output, or a report limited to unrelated findings as evidence of absence. Stopping/unknown: stop and select the negative option only when both tools complete and concordantly report absence of the named cardiovascular abnormalities and the independent report explicitly supports no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings for the same image. If these concordant-absence conditions hold, select the negative option and stop. 6) If either call fails or is unavailable, if the report is ambiguous, if the named list is incomplete, or if outputs conflict, do not infer absence. For a conflict about the same finding and image, allow at most one targeted observed verification using a registered tool; if unresolved, stop and report uncertainty rather than asserting absence."}, If the targeted answer is unclear or fails and no explicit report statement covers the structure, stop and state unknown/insufficient evidence. Stop when the targeted expert is clear and, if a report is cited, the report explicitly covers the queried structure without conflict, or when unknown/insufficient evidence is declared. Do not infer from unrelated normal findings."}

messages.content:
Convert the approved source analysis into ONE reusable procedural skill or a local patch.
Only source observations support the content. No fixed source answer, option letter, figure number or patient identity.
Trigger must specify applicability. core_action must specify observable checks, appropriate tool actions, failure/unknown
handling and when to stop; never require access to the current task's unknown reference answer.
Return JSON {"operation":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE","patch_target_id":null,"patch_section":null,"patch_content":null,
"content":{"name":"...","description":"...","applicable_conditions":"...","branch":"general|task_level|action_level",
"tool_name":null,"task_category":"provided category","required_tools":[],"risk_level":"low|medium|high","core_action":"..."}}.
For PATCH only return patch_target_id, patch_section (one content field), patch_content and operation;
do not replace unrelated sections. Scope fields branch, task_category and tool_name cannot change.
NONE may omit all other fields. Registered tools only. No invented measurements or blanket disease exclusion.

R54: Include explicit question-type/object requirements, triggering evidence,
exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.
Preserve the original nine-field content schema. Do not add fields or thresholds without source support.
If supplied reviewer feedback, perform ONE targeted repair: remove unsupported details or narrow scope.
Do not add evidence, change CREATE to PATCH or change an existing PATCH target during repair.

For laterality use an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome. A
bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone cannot resolve side. Treat
conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

negative-verification sequence. 3) For a clear negative, call maira2_grounded_report on the same image. 4) Review its findings/report for acute thoracic abnormalities; clear lungs, normal heart size, absence of acute thoracic findings, select the negative option and stop. 6) If the report is unavailable, failed, or inconclusive, or if it lists an acute thoracic finding despite the expert's NONE may omit all other fields. Registered tools only. No invented measurements or blanket disease exclusion.

exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.

Do not add evidence, change CREATE to PATCH or change an existing PATCH target during repair.

For laterality use an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome. A
bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone cannot resolve side. Treat
conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

Before querying, the expert prompt must name the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, anchored to source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification; the list must be sufficiently comprehensive for the question's scope. Required tool capabilities: a chest-radiograph expert QA model that accepts an explicit abnormality-list question, and an independent grounded-report/report-generation tool for the same image that returns a report or 'no significant findings'. Exclusions: do not apply to laterality/side questions, non-chest-radiograph images, or questions about a specific single finding where broad-system absence is not at issue. Do not use a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box to resolve side. Do not treat an incomplete abnormality list, a single negative model output, or a report limited to unrelated findings as evidence of absence. Stopping/unknown: stop and select the negative option only when both tools complete and concordantly report absence of the named cardiovascular abnormalities and the independent report explicitly supports no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings for the same image. message.content: {"operation":"PATCH","patch_target_id":"s_3efed96fb5382872","patch_section":"core_action","patch_content":"Parse the question to confirm that the object is skeletal/osseous abnormality and that the required response is yes/no presence; otherwise stop as not applicable. Call chest_xray_expert with a targeted skeletal question enumerating fractures, lytic lesions, and deformities. Inspect its response for an explicit negation of skeletal/osseous abnormality. If the response is clearly negative, call maira2_grounded_report on the same image for independent corroboration and explicitly scan the report text and every finding/box annotation for a skeletal/osseous statement. If the report contains no explicit skeletal/osseous statement, or all grounded boxes are non-skeletal, classify the report as out-of-scope, not negative: do not cite it as corroboration, do not state two-source concordance, and keep incidental non-skeletal findings such as airspace disease separate from the skeletal judgment. When the targeted expert is clearly negative and the report is out-of-scope, either perform at most one additional skeletal-scoped observed verification on the same image with a registered suitable tool, or emit the absence option based on the clear targeted expert alone without claiming report corroboration. If both the targeted expert and the grounded report independently and explicitly negate acute osseous/skeletal abnormality, answer the absence option. Do not treat incidental non-skeletal findings as skeletal abnormalities. If either source is affirmative, equivocal, fails, lacks an explicit osseous statement after the allowed verification, or the sources conflict about the same finding and image, do not claim absence from concordance; after at most one targeted observed verification, if still unresolved state unknown/uncertain when the answer format permits, otherwise avoid asserting abnormality or absence beyond the observed evidence. Stop once an explicit negative targeted expert plus either an explicit negative skeletal statement from the report or the single out-of-scope verification/negative-only path has been completed, or after the single conflict/unknown verification has been attempted and no resolution is obtained. Keep unexecuted steps as hypotheses."}

Convert the approved source analysis into ONE reusable procedural skill or a local patch.
Only source observations support the content. No fixed source answer, option letter, figure number or patient identity.
Trigger must specify applicability. core_action must specify observable checks, appropriate tool actions, failure/unknown
handling and when to stop; never require access to the current task's unknown reference answer.
Return JSON {"operation":"CREATE|PATCH|NONE","patch_target_id":null,"patch_section":null,"patch_content":null,
"content":{"name":"...","description":"...","applicable_conditions":"...","branch":"general|task_level|action_level",
"tool_name":null,"task_category":"provided category","required_tools":[],"risk_level":"low|medium|high","core_action":"..."}}.
For PATCH only return patch_target_id, patch_section (one content field), patch_content and operation;
do not replace unrelated sections. Scope fields branch, task_category and tool_name cannot change.
NONE may omit all other fields. Registered tools only. No invented measurements or blanket disease exclusion.

R54: Include explicit question-type/object requirements, triggering evidence,
exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.
Preserve the original nine-field content schema. Do not add fields or thresholds without source support.
If supplied reviewer feedback, perform ONE targeted repair: remove unsupported details or narrow scope.
Do not add evidence, change CREATE to PATCH or change an existing PATCH target during repair.

For laterality use an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome. A
bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone cannot resolve side. Treat
conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

exclusions, required tool capabilities and stopping/unknown conditions in applicable_conditions/core_action.

conflicting answers about the same finding and image as a possible trigger for
one targeted, observed verification. Keep steps that were not executed as hypotheses.

Review a candidate against the actual source trajectory, source image, existing nearest skills and tool menu.
Reject unsupported clinical specifics, rules requiring unknown current labels, copied source answers, vague reminders,
unsafe generalization or incompatible tool capabilities. A binary label does not verify all findings in a model explanation.
Return JSON {"quality":true/false,"reason":"specific source evidence or failure","duplicate_of":null or exact existing ID}.
Duplicate means same reusable operation within the same branch/scope; different conditions may require a local PATCH.
Do not approve merely because JSON is valid. You are a same-model reviewer, not an independent clinician.

R54: Check each trigger and procedural operation against the cited source steps.
Assess separately whether execution occurred and whether final correctness actually supports the operation.
An unexecuted repair is a hypothesis, not an approved skill. Reject invented thresholds, inferred findings,
and treating tool agreement as truth. Allow a narrow supported operation without requiring a broad maxim.

Reject treating a bare yes/no as resolving a two-option localization question.
Do not treat a crop or model-produced box as confirmation of a finding or side.
Check whether the cited operation actually returned evidence usable for this task.

messages.content:
Review a candidate against the actual source trajectory, source image, existing nearest skills and tool menu.
Reject unsupported clinical specifics, rules requiring unknown current labels, copied source answers, vague reminders,
unsafe generalization or incompatible tool capabilities. A binary label does not verify all findings in a model explanation.
Return JSON {"quality":true/false,"reason":"specific source evidence or failure","duplicate_of":null or exact existing ID}.
Duplicate means same reusable operation within the same branch/scope; different conditions may require a local PATCH.
Do not approve merely because JSON is valid. You are a same-model reviewer, not an independent clinician.

R54: Check each trigger and procedural operation against the cited source steps.
Assess separately whether execution occurred and whether final correctness actually supports the operation.
An unexecuted repair is a hypothesis, not an approved skill. Reject invented thresholds, inferred findings,
and treating tool agreement as truth. Allow a narrow supported operation without requiring a broad maxim.

Reject treating a bare yes/no as resolving a two-option localization question.
Do not treat a crop or model-produced box as confirmation of a finding or side.
Check whether the cited operation actually returned evidence usable for this task.

Review a candidate against the actual source trajectory, source image, existing nearest skills and tool menu.
Reject unsupported clinical specifics, rules requiring unknown current labels, copied source answers, vague reminders,
unsafe generalization or incompatible tool capabilities. A binary label does not verify all findings in a model explanation.
Return JSON {"quality":true/false,"reason":"specific source evidence or failure","duplicate_of":null or exact existing ID}.
Duplicate means same reusable operation within the same branch/scope; different conditions may require a local PATCH.
Do not approve merely because JSON is valid. You are a same-model reviewer, not an independent clinician.

R54: Check each trigger and procedural operation against the cited source steps.
Assess separately whether execution occurred and whether final correctness actually supports the operation.
An unexecuted repair is a hypothesis, not an approved skill. Reject invented thresholds, inferred findings,
and treating tool agreement as truth. Allow a narrow supported operation without requiring a broad maxim.

Reject treating a bare yes/no as resolving a two-option localization question.
Do not treat a crop or model-produced box as confirmation of a finding or side.
Check whether the cited operation actually returned evidence usable for this task.

Review a candidate against the actual source trajectory, source image, existing nearest skills and tool menu.
Reject unsupported clinical specifics, rules requiring unknown current labels, copied source answers, vague reminders,
unsafe generalization or incompatible tool capabilities. A binary label does not verify all findings in a model explanation.

Duplicate means same reusable operation within the same branch/scope; different conditions may require a local PATCH.
Do not approve merely because JSON is valid. You are a same-model reviewer, not an independent clinician.

R54: Check each trigger and procedural operation against the cited source steps.
Assess separately whether execution occurred and whether final correctness actually supports the operation.
An unexecuted repair is a hypothesis, not an approved skill. Reject invented thresholds, inferred findings,
and treating tool agreement as truth. Allow a narrow supported operation without requiring a broad maxim.

Reject treating a bare yes/no as resolving a two-option localization question.
Do not treat a crop or model-produced box as confirmation of a finding or side.
Check whether the cited operation actually returned evidence usable for this task.

Review a candidate against the actual source trajectory, source image, existing nearest skills and tool menu.
Reject unsupported clinical specifics, rules requiring unknown current labels, copied source answers, vague reminders,
unsafe generalization or incompatible tool capabilities. A binary label does not verify all findings in a model explanation.

Duplicate means same reusable operation within the same branch/scope; different conditions may require a local PATCH.
Do not approve merely because JSON is valid. You are a same-model reviewer, not an independent clinician.

R54: Check each trigger and procedural operation against the cited source steps.
Assess separately whether execution occurred and whether final correctness actually supports the operation.
An unexecuted repair is a hypothesis, not an approved skill. Reject invented thresholds, inferred findings,
and treating tool agreement as truth. Allow a narrow supported operation without requiring a broad maxim.

Reject treating a bare yes/no as resolving a two-option localization question.
Do not treat a crop or model-produced box as confirmation of a finding or side.
Check whether the cited operation actually returned evidence usable for this task.
